newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA NIPS ALPHAND TO WIN DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-GHEDINA NIPS ALPHAND TO WIN DOWNHILL.

text.p: Italy's Kristian Ghedina collected his third win of the season and second in succession by pipping French rival Luc Alphand by 13 hundredths of a second in a World Cup downhill on Saturday.

Ghedina roared down the 4.2-kms Lauberhorn course, the longest on the World Cup circuit, in a course record time of two minutes, 24.23 seconds to register the seventh win of his career and was unshaken after falling and crashing head-first into the padded barriers beyond the finish line.
Alphand, still shaken by teammate Adrien Duvillard's serious crash during final training on Friday, was able to hold his concentration long enough to take second in 2:24.36.
Fritz Strobl of Austria, the only other skier other than Ghedina or Alphand to win a World Cup downhill this season, was third in 2:24.62.

Alphand, the reigning World Cup downhill champion and Ghedina, who became the most successful World Cup downhiller in Italian ski history with his win last weekend in Chamonix, began the day deadlocked atop the downhill standings.
But the 27-year-old Italian will now head to next weekend's downhill doubleheader in Kitzbuehel with a slim 20-point advantage on the Frenchman.
The race was delayed 30 minutes when American Kyle Rasmussen, a winner on the same course in 1995, went off midway through his run and had to be airlifted from the course by helicopter.
The extent of Rasmussen's injuries were not immediately known.
